newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgarian coins worth more as scrap, paper says.
newsitem.headline: Bulgarian coins worth more as scrap, paper says.

text.p: A Bulgarian newspaper warned on Friday that lev coins could disappear from circulation because the currency's collapse meant they were worth more as scrap metal.
"Levs are more valuable by the kilo," said a story in Kontinent, quoting coin collecters as saying one, two, five and 10 lev coins were being melted down by traders.
Increasing poverty caused by the collapse of the lev has brought Bulgarians onto the streets for 11 consecutive days of protests to demand a general election.

Kontinent said one kg (2.2 lb) of one lev coins was worth twice its face value. It calculated that if the central bank recalled the 205 million one lev coins in circulation and sold them at London Metal Exchange prices, it would make a profit of 188.64 million levs ($293,300).
"Traders are buying copper at 600 to 800 levs per kilo. On the other hand for one kilo of copper 250 to 300 one lev coins can be made," it said.
It said Bulgaria had suffered the same problem before -- at the end of World War One and during World War Two.
The central bank fixed the lev sharply lower on Friday at 682.11 to the dollar from 642.69 on Thursday. A year ago, the lev was trading at about 70 to the dollar. ($1=642.69 Leva)
